eventMetadata.context_description:
**Minnesota Lynx (31-8, 1st in West) visit the Atlanta Dream (25-14, top of East contention) on August 30 at Gateway Center Arena.** The Lynx enter with the league’s best record and a dominant 17-2 road mark, riding an eight-game road win streak despite a recent 80-66 home loss to the Golden State Valkyries that snapped a longer streak. Atlanta sits at 12-7 at home but dropped its last outing 101-83 to the Portland Fire.

Key context centers on roster health and recent form. Minnesota is missing starter Courtney Williams (lower leg, day-to-day) while relying on rookie Olivia Miles for playmaking (roughly 6+ assists and strong scoring) alongside Natasha Howard and Napheesa Collier. Atlanta plays without Brionna Jones (leg) and has listed DeWanna Bonner out for rest, leaning on Angel Reese’s rebounding dominance, Jordin Canada’s assist leadership, and perimeter scoring from Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray.

The teams have split prior meetings this season, with Minnesota taking the most recent 96-81 win. Lynx depth, defensive efficiency, and road success give them the stronger profile entering the contest, while Atlanta’s home environment and interior presence offer counter opportunities. Late scratches, rest decisions, and any further injury updates could shift availability ahead of tip-off.
